L1_scale.finding: measured: conflict resolution and full-context serialization stay fast to 10k records (0.03s/0.04s) — read-path latency is NOT the binding constraint at personal scale. The binding constraint is PROMPT TOKENS, not lookup time (measured in the cost experiment): serializing 100k memories is cheap in ms and unaffordable in tokens

L2_contradictions.finding: contradictory inferred memories are silently RANKED, not detected: newest/highest-confidence wins with no flag to the user. Contradiction detection needs a Layer-2 advisory flag — noted as future work

L3_implicit_staleness.finding: PROVABLE LIMITATION confirmed: a fact that goes stale with no signal remains active indefinitely. The layer cannot detect implicit staleness; it can only make staleness correctable when a signal arrives

L4_poisoning.finding: injected content is quarantined by TAGGING (inferred + low confidence + source-traceable to the exact turn), but NOT by default blocked: the store accepts any inferred write. Defense-in-depth (blocklist predicates, e.g. credentials) is a policy the spec leaves to deployments — reported as an open hardening item

L5_leakage.finding: read path is clean (proof-of-absence PASS) but payload persists in append-only history.jsonl and in the raw session turn. Boundary CONFIRMED: the guarantee is 'absent from later prompts', not 'erased from history'. Full erasure requires cascading into session_log tombstones — spec §5.3 carve-out, paper reports this plainly

L6_ambiguous_correction.finding: the protocol REQUIRES a resolvable target_id; a vague correction ('that's not what I meant') cannot be bound without an agent-side resolution step. The unbindable class exists and is reported; resolution heuristics are agent work (Layer 5+), not memory-layer guarantees

L7_invalidation_cost.finding: a 300-deep dependent chain re-flags in 1.351s with per-flag full-file rewrites (O(depth^2)) — above an interactive budget; the shipped batched rewrite (single O(n) pass) does it in 0.034s. Both numbers are persisted and reported

L8_tamper.finding: naive tampering is ALWAYS caught (hash chain). Tampering WITH chain recomputation is NEVER caught — the uncatchable class, mirroring Qafiya's provable limits. Mitigation (external hash anchoring) is future work, stated in the paper
